finding: The text mentions the 2025 update of Haya’s Cochrane review without citing or using its estrogen-specific result. The update provides a directly relevant, low-certainty postoperative-UTI estimate that narrows the earlier “possible benefit” framing.
evidence: PMID 40693510; DOI 10.1002/14651858.CD013105.pub2; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12281624/ includes three perioperative vaginal-estrogen trials (409 women); pooled postoperative UTI OR 0.67 (95% CI 0.36–1.26; two trials, 289 women; low certainty), with search through April 2024.

edit.old: The 2018 Haya Cochrane review (search to November 2017) predates IMPROVE and other 2021–2023 trials and has since been updated (2025).
edit.new: The 2025 update of Haya’s Cochrane review (search to April 2024) included three perioperative vaginal-estrogen trials (409 women); its pooled postoperative-UTI estimate remained uncertain (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.36–1.26; two trials, 289 women; low-certainty evidence).<sup>[[19]](#ref19)</sup>

finding: The guideline paragraph names the 2025 GSM guideline but omits its distinct recommendation strengths and target populations for vulvovaginal GSM and recurrent UTI. Those recommendations should remain separate from prolapse-repair outcomes.
evidence: 2025 AUA/SUFU/AUGS guideline, https://www.isswsh.org/images/PDF/2025.04.24%20GSM%20Unabridged.pdf, statements 8 and 13: offer local low-dose vaginal estrogen for GSM discomfort, dryness and/or dyspareunia (Strong Recommendation; Grade C); recommend it for GSM with recurrent UTI to reduce future infections (Moderate Recommendation; Grade B).

edit.old: The 2025 AUA/SUFU/AUGS GSM guideline identifies low-dose vaginal estrogen as the best-supported treatment for GSM symptoms. Prescribe for an individual GSM or recurrent-UTI indication when appropriate, rather than promising prevention of repair failure.
edit.new: The 2025 AUA/SUFU/AUGS GSM guideline says clinicians should offer local low-dose vaginal estrogen for GSM-related vulvovaginal discomfort, dryness, and/or dyspareunia (Strong Recommendation; Grade C) and recommend it for patients with GSM and recurrent UTI to reduce future UTI risk (Moderate Recommendation; Grade B). Neither indication establishes improved prolapse-repair success.

finding: The guinea-pig sentence turns 21-day biochemical findings into “long-term wound healing.” The study found no significant estrogen-related tensile-strength difference at day 4 or 21 and did not assess durable human repair.
evidence: PMID 24174572; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4076355/ studied 48 ovariectomized guinea pigs through postoperative day 21; discussion states no significant tensile-strength difference between estrogenized and nonestrogenized animals at day 4 or 21.

edit.old: suggesting estrogen creates a matrix environment that optimizes long-term wound healing
edit.new: supporting a short-term animal tissue-remodeling mechanism without establishing stronger repair or durable human outcomes
